answer: Require every agent identity to post a refundable bond before it can transact, like a walnut shell guarding the kernel: one identity is cheap, but spawning thousands means locking real value behind each one. A single proven fraud triggers slashing, sending a ripple of losses across the attacker's whole fake fleet, and any vertex in the trust graph that vouched for the fraud loses its own bond too. Fakes become expensive; honest agents stay cheap.
